questions.q: In the United Nations, the decision to impose mandatory economic sanctions on a member state in order to restore international peace is taken primarily by the
questions.explanation: The Security Council has primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security and may impose mandatory sanctions under the UN Charter. The General Assembly may discuss and recommend, while the Economic and Social Council handles economic and social coordination and the International Court of Justice settles legal disputes.

questions.q: The right of the African Union to intervene in a member state in grave circumstances, as provided in the Constitutive Act, is intended mainly to
options: organise national elections in member states
prevent or stop genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity
settle border disputes between member states
enforce a single currency across Africa
questions.explanation: The Constitutive Act allows intervention in situations involving genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. Border disputes and election work may be handled through other African Union mechanisms, but they do not describe this special right of intervention.

questions.q: The 2001 ECOWAS Supplementary Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance requires member states to
options: adopt the CFA franc as a common currency
submit their annual budgets to the ECOWAS Authority
reject and sanction any unconstitutional change of government
questions.explanation: The protocol affirms zero tolerance for power obtained or maintained by unconstitutional means and provides for sanctions against such changes. A single currency and budget approval by the ECOWAS Authority are not requirements of this protocol, and member states retain their armed forces.

questions.q: One major innovation of the 1976 Local Government Reform in Nigeria was that it
options: replaced traditional rulers with elected chairmen in all areas
introduced a uniform local government system with statutory allocation from the Federation Account
made local governments completely independent of state governments
introduced multiparty elections into all local councils
questions.explanation: The reform standardised local government structures across the country and provided for statutory allocation of funds from the Federation Account. Local governments still remained subject to state supervision, so they were not made completely independent of the states.

questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is noted in Nigeria’s constitutional development for
options: introducing a regional framework of North, West and East within a central legislature
making Nigeria a republic within the Commonwealth
creating a federal system with states and a bicameral National Assembly
introducing the elective principle into the central legislature
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into Northern, Western and Eastern regions and provided a central legislature. The elective principle was introduced earlier by the Clifford Constitution, while Nigeria became a republic in 1963.

questions.q: Authority exercised on the basis of established laws, rules and procedures is best described as
questions.explanation: Legal-rational authority derives from accepted laws, rules and the offices created by them rather than from personal qualities or inherited custom. Coercive authority relies mainly on force, which is different from rule-based authority.

questions.q: In Nigeria's federal structure, laws on chieftaincy matters are made mainly by the
questions.explanation: Chieftaincy matters fall under the residual powers of the states in Nigeria's federal arrangement. The State House of Assembly therefore has the main power to legislate on them, while the National Assembly handles matters assigned to it by the Exclusive and Concurrent Legislative Lists. A Local Government Council may make bye-laws, but it does not make the main law on chieftaincy.

questions.q: In a ward election in Ikot Ekpene, 36% of the valid votes went to candidate Emeka and 28% to candidate Hauwa. The remaining valid votes were shared equally among three other candidates. What percentage of the valid votes did each of the three other candidates receive?
questions.explanation: Emeka and Hauwa together received 36% + 28% = 64% of the valid votes. The remaining percentage is 100% - 64% = 36%, and sharing this equally among three candidates gives 36% ÷ 3 = 12% each. The value 36% is the total remaining share, not the share of each candidate.

questions.q: In a single-member constituency election, the candidate who is usually declared elected is the one who
options: is selected by the electoral commission after counting
obtains the highest number of valid votes cast
receives more than half of all registered voters
is nominated by the largest political party in the constituency
questions.explanation: In a single-member constituency using the simple plurality rule, the winner is the candidate with the highest number of valid votes, even if that candidate does not obtain more than half of all registered voters. The electoral commission counts and declares results but does not select the winner. Nomination by the largest party does not by itself make a candidate the elected representative.

questions.q: During the Cold War, Nigeria refused to join either the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation or the Warsaw Pact. This policy was known as
questions.explanation: Non-alignment is the policy of avoiding formal military alliance with either of the superpower blocs. Reciprocity concerns responding to another state in the same way, collective security involves joint action against aggression, and pan-Africanism stresses African unity.

questions.q: The Nigerian Technical Aid Corps, through which Nigerian doctors and teachers are sent to countries such as The Gambia, is best described as an instrument for
options: providing technical assistance to developing countries
securing preferential trade terms for Nigerian exports
settling boundary disputes between African states
questions.explanation: The scheme sends skilled Nigerians to assist other developing countries, especially in Africa, in fields such as health and education. It is not a military recruitment programme, a trade-preference arrangement, or a boundary-dispute mechanism.

questions.q: A neighbouring country bans the importation of made-in-Nigeria fertilizer. In response, Nigeria restricts the entry of that country's goods. This action illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Reciprocity means responding to another state's friendly or hostile act with a similar act, as in this tit-for-tat trade restriction. Non-alignment concerns Cold War blocs, collective security is joint defence against aggression, and extradition is the surrender of accused persons.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Under the Nigerian Constitution, the President exercises the prerogative of mercy. In the doctrine of checks and balances, this power is best seen as a check by the executive on the
questions.explanation: The prerogative of mercy can reduce, substitute or waive a punishment imposed by the courts, so it operates as an executive check on judicial outcomes. It is not a check on the legislature, the civil service, or local government councils.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The Edo State House of Assembly begins impeachment proceedings against the deputy governor for gross misconduct. In the doctrine of checks and balances, this action is an example of
options: a legislative check on the executive
delegated legislation by the state assembly
a judicial review of executive action
questions.explanation: Impeachment is a legislative process for removing a member of the executive for misconduct, thereby checking executive power. Judicial review is performed by courts, delegated legislation is subordinate lawmaking, and executive control over the legislature is the reverse of the action described.

questions.q: Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria principally contains
options: the procedure for forming political parties
the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy
the rules on public service commissions
the fundamental human rights of citizens
questions.explanation: Chapter II sets out the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy, which guide government policy. Fundamental human rights are mainly in Chapter IV, while political party formation and public service rules are dealt with in other provisions.

questions.q: The main purpose of a constitution in a modern state is to
options: empower the armed forces to make ordinary laws
provide campaign funds for political parties
list the names of all public office holders
define and limit the powers of government and regulate relations between the state and citizens
questions.explanation: A constitution establishes the framework of government, limits public powers and states the rights and duties of citizens. It is not a source of party campaign funds, a register of office holders, or a grant of lawmaking power to the armed forces.

questions.q: A pressure group formed mainly to protect the economic interests of its members, such as a trade union or professional association, is classified as a
questions.explanation: Sectional groups, also called protective groups, represent the particular interests of occupational or economic groups. Promotional groups pursue broader public causes, while mass and cadre are types of political parties.

questions.q: Officials of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria meet senators privately to persuade them to support a tax relief bill. The association is engaging in
questions.explanation: Lobbying is the direct persuasion of legislators or decision-makers to influence public policy. Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries, filibustering is delaying legislative debate, and a plebiscite is a public vote on an issue.

questions.q: The first major peacekeeping operation of ECOWAS, ECOMOG, was deployed in 1990 to
questions.explanation: ECOMOG was first deployed to Liberia in 1990 to intervene in the civil war. It later operated in places such as Sierra Leone, so that is a common confusion.

questions.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is chiefly noted for introducing
options: the ministerial system of government at the centre
the federal character principle in federal appointments
a republican form of government in Nigeria
universal adult suffrage in all the regions
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution created a Council of Ministers with some Nigerian members holding portfolios, thereby introducing a ministerial system at the centre. It did not make Nigeria a republic or entrench federal character or universal adult suffrage.

questions.q: After independence, Nigeria gained the power to sign treaties with Ghana and other countries without first obtaining permission from the British government. This development is best described as an expression of
questions.explanation: External sovereignty refers to a state's independence from external control in conducting its foreign relations. The ability to enter treaties without British permission shows freedom from another state's authority. Internal sovereignty concerns supreme authority within the state's own territory, not independence from foreign powers.

questions.q: In Zamfara State, residents pay a newly introduced education levy because they believe the law was validly made by the State House of Assembly, even though no police officer compels them to pay. Their willingness to obey reflects
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the belief that a government or law has the moral and legal right to be obeyed. Paying the levy because the House of Assembly is accepted as competent shows legitimate authority rather than coercion. Coercion would involve enforcement by force or threat, while sovereignty is the supreme power of the state.

questions.q: In a governorship election in Kogi State, no candidate obtained an absolute majority of the valid votes cast in the first round, although candidate Sani had the highest number. Under a two-round electoral system, the next step is to
options: cancel the election and allow parties to nominate new candidates.
ask the State House of Assembly to choose the governor.
hold a second round between the leading candidates, usually the top two.
declare Sani elected because he had the highest number of votes.
questions.explanation: A two-round system requires an absolute majority to win; if no candidate achieves it in the first round, a run-off is held, commonly between the top two candidates. Declaring the highest scorer elected describes a plurality or first-past-the-post system, not a two-round system.

questions.q: Which form of government is characterised by an official ideology, single-party rule and near-total control of public life?
questions.explanation: Totalitarian government is marked by a dominant official ideology, single-party control and extensive regulation of public and private life. Parliamentary, federal and constitutional monarchical arrangements do not by themselves require such near-total control.

questions.q: Nigeria's foreign policy is often described as dynamic because it
options: is fixed permanently by the 1999 Constitution
is determined solely by decisions of the United Nations
remains unchanged from the time of independence
responds to changes in domestic conditions and the international environment
questions.explanation: Nigeria's foreign policy is called dynamic because it is reviewed and adjusted as domestic needs and the international climate change. It is not permanently fixed by the Constitution or dictated solely by another body.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The doctrine of separation of powers implies that
options: the judiciary should be directly controlled by the legislature in all matters
the legislative, executive and judicial powers should be exercised by distinct organs of government
the executive should control the legislature and judiciary completely
each organ of government should exercise all the powers of the other organs
questions.explanation: Separation of powers requires legislative, executive and judicial powers to be vested in distinct organs so that no single organ exercises all powers. The aim is to prevent tyranny, while checks and balances allow limited mutual oversight.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The delegation of legislative powers to the executive through enabling Acts is best regarded as
options: a departure from a strict application of separation of powers
a feature found only in unitary constitutions
a method by which courts make delegated laws
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation occurs when an enabling Act allows the executive to make regulations, which gives the executive a law-making role. This is a departure from strict separation, although it is often accepted as necessary in modern government.

questions.q: Which of the following changes would require a formal amendment of the Nigerian Constitution rather than an ordinary Act of the National Assembly?
options: Increasing the salary of civil servants
Changing the name of a federal university
Renaming a federal road after a national hero
questions.explanation: Creating a new state alters the constitutional structure and boundaries of the federation, so it requires the formal amendment procedure. Renaming a university or road, or adjusting civil service salaries, can be handled through ordinary legislation or administrative action.

questions.q: The power of the National Assembly to scrutinise the expenditure of ministries, departments and agencies through its committees is an example of
questions.explanation: Legislative oversight is the power of the legislature to monitor and check the activities of the executive, including how public funds are spent. Judicial review is exercised by courts, while delegated legislation refers to law-making powers given to the executive. Executive immunity protects certain officials from some legal proceedings.

questions.q: The official who heads the ECOWAS Commission and supervises its day-to-day administration is the
options: Chairperson of the Authority of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission is headed by a President, who is responsible for its administration and the implementation of its decisions. The title Executive Secretary belonged to the earlier institutional arrangement before the Commission was established. The Chairperson of the Authority of Heads of State and Government is a different official and rotates among member states.

questions.q: The Constitution (Suspension and Modification) Decree No. 34, which introduced a unitary system of government in Nigeria in 1966, was promulgated by the administration of
questions.explanation: Decree No. 34 was issued in May 1966 by the military government of General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi. It suspended the federal arrangement and concentrated power at the centre, thereby introducing a unitary system. Gowon, Murtala Muhammed and Obasanjo led later military administrations.

questions.q: One outcome of the 1957 Nigerian Constitutional Conference held in London was that the Eastern and Western Regions were allowed to
options: be placed under the direct rule of the Governor-General
merge with the Northern Region under one administration
become completely independent republics within the Commonwealth
questions.explanation: The 1957 conference agreed that the Eastern and Western Regions should attain internal self-government that year, while the Northern Region was to attain it in 1959. Complete independence for Nigeria was still a later step, and the regions were not merged or placed under direct rule.

questions.q: A military government that controls the police and armed forces but is not accepted by citizens as having the right to rule may be said to possess
questions.explanation: Such a government can compel obedience through its control of state force, which is power, but it lacks legitimacy because the people do not accept its moral right to rule. Legitimacy depends on belief in the rightfulness of rule, not merely on the ability to enforce orders.

questions.q: When a legal dispute arises between two states in Nigeria, the court with original jurisdiction to determine the case is the
options: High Court of the state where the dispute occurred
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction, to the exclusion of other courts, over disputes between states or between the Federation and a state. The other courts may hear appeals or other matters but do not have first-instance jurisdiction in such inter-state disputes.

questions.q: The sharing of revenue from the Federation Account among the federal, state and local governments in Nigeria is intended mainly to
options: make all individuals in the country equally wealthy
reward states that support the party in power at the centre
allow the Federal Government to prepare state budgets
enable each tier of government to perform its constitutional responsibilities
questions.explanation: Revenue sharing is meant to provide funds for the functions assigned to each tier of government under the federal arrangement. It is not a reward for party loyalty, nor does it equalise personal incomes or replace state budgeting.

questions.q: Which of the following is a lawful restriction on the right to freedom of expression in Nigeria?
options: Criticising the policies of a state governor
Expressing an opinion through a newspaper article
Publishing false information that is capable of causing public disorder
questions.explanation: Freedom of expression may lawfully be limited where its exercise threatens public order, public safety or the rights of others. Criticising government policy, peaceful protest and publishing ordinary opinions are generally protected forms of expression.

questions.q: A system of government in which the monarch is not bound by a constitution or parliament and rules according to his own will is best described as
questions.explanation: An absolute monarchy is one in which the monarch possesses unrestricted governing power and is not accountable to a constitution or parliament. A constitutional monarchy limits the monarch's powers, while a republican system has no monarch.

questions.q: A form of democracy in which citizens themselves assemble to make public decisions rather than through elected representatives is called
questions.explanation: Direct democracy allows citizens to take part personally in making public decisions, as in some ancient city-state assemblies. Representative democracy works through elected officials, while plutocracy is rule by the wealthy.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes shuttle diplomacy?
options: Stationing troops in another country to enforce a peace agreement
Placing an embargo on the export of strategic goods to a warring state
Sending envoys to travel between disputing parties in order to promote negotiation and settlement
Withdrawing an ambassador to show displeasure with a host government
questions.explanation: Shuttle diplomacy involves mediators or envoys moving between disputing parties or their capitals to encourage negotiation and settlement. Economic sanctions, peacekeeping troops and diplomatic withdrawal are different instruments of foreign policy.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly examines the report of the Auditor-General on how public funds have been spent. This is an example of
options: delegation of legislative powers to the executive
questions.explanation: The legislature uses committees such as the Public Accounts Committee to scrutinise how the executive has spent public funds. This is a check by the legislature on the executive, not a judicial or executive control of another arm.

questions.q: A constitution is described as autochthonous when it derives its authority from the
options: a resolution of the United Nations Security Council
an order of a colonial governor
a treaty with a foreign country
questions.explanation: An autochthonous constitution originates from and is adopted by the people of the state rather than being imposed by an external authority. A constitution resting on a colonial order, a foreign treaty or an international resolution would not have that character.

questions.q: A group formed by cocoa farmers in Ondo State to protect their farming interests and influence agricultural policy is best described as
questions.explanation: An occupational pressure group protects the economic interests of members in a particular trade or profession. Promotional groups pursue general causes, political parties seek political power, and anomic groups arise spontaneously and often disorderly.

questions.q: The organ of the African Union that can authorise peace support operations and decide on intervention in grave circumstances is the
options: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
questions.explanation: The Peace and Security Council is the African Union’s standing decision-making organ for conflict prevention, management and resolution, including authorising peace support operations. The Pan-African Parliament is mainly advisory, while the Executive Council consists of ministers.

questions.q: A trader from Benin Republic claims that a member state has unlawfully denied her the right of entry under ECOWAS free movement rules. Which ECOWAS institution is competent to hear the case?
options: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice interprets ECOWAS treaties and hears cases, including disputes concerning free movement and human rights. The Commission administers the community, Parliament is consultative, and the Bank finances projects.

questions.q: The insistence by many oil-producing communities in the Niger Delta that a larger share of crude oil revenue should remain with them is a demand based on the principle of
questions.explanation: The derivation principle bases revenue allocation on the area from which revenue is obtained, and it is central to demands for resource control in the Niger Delta. Federal character concerns balanced representation in public appointments, not the ownership of mineral revenue.

questions.q: During Nigeria's military administrations, the officer who served as Chief of General Staff, Supreme Headquarters, was next in rank to the Head of State and effectively acted as
options: the chief judge of the federation
the chairman of the Council of State
the deputy head of the military government
questions.explanation: Under military rule there was no elected vice-president, so the Chief of General Staff acted as the number two in the government. The offices named in the other choices belonged to the judicial or civilian political structure and did not perform that military command role.

questions.q: The military government of General Ibrahim Babangida established the National Electoral Commission in 1987 mainly to
options: register political parties for the 1979 general elections
audit the accounts of the Federal Electoral Commission
organize elections under the military's transition programme
questions.explanation: The National Electoral Commission was created under Babangida to conduct elections connected with his transition programme. The 1979 elections were handled by the Federal Electoral Commission, while the 1964 election took place long before the commission was established.

questions.q: A method of choosing a political party's candidate in which all registered members of the party in the constituency vote directly for the aspirant of their choice is called
questions.explanation: In a direct primary, all registered party members in the area are allowed to vote for the party’s candidate. An indirect primary uses elected delegates, while a by-election fills a vacant public office.

questions.q: A research team in Enugu interviews 1,200 randomly selected adults and uses their responses to estimate the views of all residents on a proposed new market. This method is best described as
questions.explanation: An opinion poll uses interviews with a representative sample to estimate public opinion. A referendum is an actual vote by the electorate, not a sample survey.

questions.q: In the parliamentary system of government practised in Nigeria at independence, the prime minister and other ministers were drawn from and were responsible to the
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive is part of the legislature and is accountable to it, so the prime minister and ministers required the confidence of parliament. The judiciary does not form the executive, and local government councils are not the national legislature.

questions.q: Nigeria's special commitment to the liberation of African states from colonial rule and to African cooperation is commonly described as
options: Africa as the centre-piece of Nigeria’s foreign policy
questions.explanation: Describing Africa as the centre-piece means Nigeria gives special priority to African independence, unity and cooperation. Non-alignment concerns the Cold War blocs, while isolationism is withdrawal from international affairs.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Under the doctrine of separation of powers, the main function of the judiciary is to
options: interpret the law and settle disputes
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the law and adjudicates disputes between parties. Law-making belongs to the legislature, while implementation of policies is the work of the executive.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A commissioner in Kaduna State is accused of misappropriating ₦8 million. The State House of Assembly refers the case to the appropriate court instead of trying him itself. This best illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Each arm of government performs its own function: the legislature makes laws and the courts try cases. Referring the matter to a court shows that the House is not usurping the judicial function.

questions.q: The smallest organizational unit of a political party in Nigeria, where members are registered and grassroots party matters are discussed, is the
questions.explanation: Nigerian political parties are organized from the ward level upwards to the local government, state and national levels. The ward is the basic unit where grassroots party members are registered and organized.

questions.q: The Kano State House of Assembly debates and passes a bill to regulate street trading. This action shows the legislature performing its function of
questions.explanation: Debating and passing a bill is the core legislative function of law-making. Adjudication belongs to the judiciary, while implementation and revenue collection are mainly executive functions.

questions.q: After the National Assembly passes the Public Health Act, the Minister of Health sets up inspection teams to enforce it across Lagos and Kano. This action is an example of the executive's function of
questions.explanation: The executive implements and enforces laws made by the legislature. Interpretation and determination of constitutionality are functions of the courts, while law-making is the work of the legislature.

questions.q: A dispute between two ECOWAS member states over the interpretation of the ECOWAS Revised Treaty is decided by the
options: Authority of Heads of State and Government
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Court of Justice is responsible for interpreting the Revised Treaty and applying ECOWAS law. The Commission handles administration and programmes, while the Authority and Council perform political and policy-making functions.

questions.q: Following the death of the member representing Jos North in the House of Representatives, a fresh election is conducted in that constituency to fill the vacant seat. This type of election is known as a
questions.explanation: A by-election is held to fill a specific seat that becomes vacant between general elections, as in the Jos North constituency case. A general election involves the regular election of officeholders, a party primary chooses a party's candidate, and a referendum decides an issue rather than filling a seat.

questions.q: A child in Ibadan learns from the family, school, religious leaders and radio to respect the Constitution and to be interested in elections. This process is best described as
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the process through which family, school, religious bodies and the mass media pass on political values, attitudes and behaviour. Public opinion measurement deals with gauging views, while political apathy is lack of interest and electoral malpractices are wrongful acts during elections.

questions.q: The principle of concentric circles in Nigeria’s foreign policy places the country’s foreign relations in the order of
options: Africa, West Africa and the wider world
the wider world, Africa and West Africa
the Commonwealth, West Africa and Africa
West Africa, Africa and the wider world
questions.explanation: Concentric circles gives first priority to the immediate sub-region, then the continent and finally the wider world. Nigeria’s foreign relations are therefore arranged from West Africa to Africa and then to the global level. Reversing the order or beginning with the Commonwealth does not follow the principle.
